text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- A new leadership for Creditanstalt, which has just been taken over by Bank Austria, is currently the most pressing issue on the agenda.
- Standard & Poor's confirmed Bank Austria's ratings at AAA, however the outlook is negative.
- The concept for the future of GiroCredit should be ready by the summer.
- U.S. papermaker Mead's plans to build a carton factory in southern Austria have been scrapped due to high investment costs.
- Far-right Freedom Party harshly criticised the conservative People's Party for its role in the sale of Creditanstalt during a special session of parliament.
- The insolvency of grocery chain Konsum two years ago might cost banks another 100 million schillings.
- The European Commission stands by its demand that the motorway fee for the Brenner pass must be abolished.
DIE PRESSE

- Rumours are heating up over who will head Creditanstalt. Possible candidates are GiroCredit boss and former Finance Minister Ferdinand Lacina, former Finance Minister and former Creditanstalt head Hannes Androsch or Die Erste savings bank's chief executive Andreas Treichl.

- Even though a merger of Bank Austria's and Creditanstalt's building groups is unlikely, Vienna's former finance chief and current chairman of the board of contractor Porr Hans Mayr expects Porr, Wibeba (both owned by Bank Austria) and Universale (owned by Creditanstalt) to cooperate closely together.

- Provincial energy provider EVN wants to take over a stake in local OKA. EVN chief executive Rudolf Gruber expects the reorganisation of Austria's electricity industry will be brought about by the market, not the economics ministry.

- Even though Austria is expected to achieve the Maastricht criteria this year, the country will have to work hard to hold the deficit level in the years to come, economic research institute Wifo said.
KURIER
- U.S. women's organisations are threatening to boycott Vienna's famous philharmonic orchestra should it not take on female musicians.
- Bank Austria and Creditanstalt have 1,700 employees in Eastern Europe with a balance sheet total of 40 billion schillings and three billion schillings of own cash.
- Bank Austria and Creditanstalt will have to reorganise their branches in Vienna to work more efficiently.
- Tyrolean Airways has ordered new planes worth 1.6 billion schillings from Canada's Bombardier.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Die Erste savings bank will play a key role in the reorganisation of Austria's banking industry.
